solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A 'monsieur' (not English) read in translation?

indicators.note: putting words into another language turns them about, so these letters are rearranged
E is the standard abbreviation for English, so that letter is dropped from the French title

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a French gentleman's title might come out if read in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' removes the E from MONSIEUR; A + MONSIUR + READ is then rearranged. The whole clue also describes the answer: a French man of letters, read by English speakers in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: André Maurois was a French novelist and biographer, a monsieur whose books English readers met in translation.

clue.text: Deans may get drunk when church remembers its saints

indicators.note: drunk people are disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cathedral deans hit the bottle on feast days.
explanation.definitionFit: A name day is the feast of the saint one is named after, a day the church commemorates its saints.

clue.text: Examine topless dress

indicators.note: the top (first) letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to probe is to examine closely

explanation.surface: An inspector checks out a topless outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless dress' reads as one phrase; 'topless' acts on the word for examine and 'dress' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose garment, a dress or gown.

clue.text: Bloke entertains duke coming in to give orders

indicators.note: the abbreviation for duke is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a bloke is a man
amuses means entertains

explanation.surface: A man hosts a visiting aristocrat who arrives to issue commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' looks like a container signal; here it is simply a synonym piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandamus is a writ from a higher court commanding someone to perform a duty, so these are legal orders.

clue.text: Call nude 'silly' having no bottoms on, exposing everything?

indicators.note: silly means daft, so these letters are jumbled
in a down clue the last letter of each word is its bottom, so each word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses nudity as silly while wearing no trousers, revealing all.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL and NUD, the two words without their last letters, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means naked, wearing no clothes, and so showing all of one's body.

clue.text: Old relations not at home in Scotland — foreign island looked for

parts.note: kin are one's relations
awa is the Scots form of away, meaning not at home

explanation.surface: A Scot searched abroad for long-lost relatives who were not at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is a Japanese island, scene of a major Second World War battle.

clue.text: Disease? There's mark left unfortunately, always

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: things gone wrong are out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: An illness that, sadly, leaves a permanent mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is a bacterial infection with a red rash, chiefly affecting children.

clue.text: One unlikely to fly over a long time? Yes and no maybe!

definitions.text: One unlikely to fly over a long time? Yes and no maybe!

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a pig, from the saying 'pigs might fly' for something that will never happen
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A riddle about a creature that may or may not take to the air for long.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail comment asks whether this bird flies far: yes, and maybe not, since some racing birds fly only short distances.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is a bird, so it does fly, though part of its name refers to an animal that famously cannot.

clue.text: Compact art form given a change of direction

indicators.note: left becomes right: the L (left) in the word for the art form is swapped for R (right)

parts.note: film, the cinema, is counted among the arts

explanation.surface: A critic remarks that some concise art form has been steered a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the usual abbreviations for left and right, so a change of direction swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact as an adjective means solid and tightly packed, a synonym of firm.

clue.text: One prominent feature in British Academy — not the stuff for ordinary mugs

definitions.text: not the stuff for ordinary mugs

indicators.note: the first pieces sit inside the abbreviation for the academy

parts.note: BA is the abbreviation for the British Academy
taken as written
a chin is a prominent feature of the face

explanation.surface: A grand member of a learned society looks down on common mug-drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mugs' tempts you towards fools; it is the drinking vessels, and fine porcelain is too good for everyday ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone china is a delicate porcelain used for best cups, not the material of everyday mugs.

clue.text: What would offer an element of reliability?

definitions.text: What would offer an element of reliability?

parts.words: What would offer an element of reliability?
parts.note: the element is the metal gold, and a reliable benchmark of quality is called by this phrase

explanation.surface: A question about what supplies a measure of dependability.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a monetary system backed by the yellow metal, and figuratively any benchmark of top quality.

clue.text: Ham? Party has too much to begin with

indicators.note: says the word for excess comes first, ahead of the party

parts.note: over means excessively, as in over-eager
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: At a party someone serves ham and overindulges at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like meat; it is the verb, to act with exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to act in an exaggerated way, which is to exaggerate or overplay a part.

clue.text: Finds much amusement with old Arabs in college?

indicators.note: the Arabs are placed inside the college

parts.note: a hall is a college or residence at a university
Saba (Sheba) was an ancient Arabian kingdom, so its people are old Arabs

explanation.surface: Students of ancient Arabian civilisation are enjoying themselves at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Saba, the biblical Sheba, was an ancient kingdom in south-west Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for having a great time or enjoying oneself hugely; the phrase is singular, so 'finds' fits it.

clue.text: Bird hurting without tail and restricted

indicators.note: the word and is held in, enclosed by the shortened word
the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: smarting means stinging or hurting

explanation.surface: A bird in pain with no tail feathers is confined to a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand martin is a small brown swallow-like bird that nests in sandbanks.

clue.text: Cross-dresser has upset nun already

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in women's clothes has already shocked a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Danny La Rue was a famous British female impersonator and drag artist of stage and television.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated drag performer, an entertainer who dressed as a woman.

clue.text: Philosopher offers jargon for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience gets is heard, so the word for jargon is said aloud

parts.note: cant is the special jargon of a group

explanation.surface: A thinker hands out technical lingo to his listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the German Enlightenment philosopher who wrote the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Satellite still moving in (roughly) a circle

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the other two pieces

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly
the letter O is shaped like a circle

indicators.note: moving means stirring, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A moon orbits, still travelling in a rough circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large moons of Jupiter, a natural satellite.

clue.text: Pitch is where it should happen

definitions.meaning: to pitch is to throw or fling
the coin flip deciding who bats first in cricket takes place on the pitch

explanation.surface: A groundsman insists that the field is the proper place for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch is to throw; and the cricket captains' pre-match coin flip happens out on the playing pitch.

clue.text: Wicketkeeper lets tons drop — one expected to take loads

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for tons falls lower in the word

parts.note: a stumper is cricket slang for the wicketkeeper, who stumps batsmen

explanation.surface: A cricket wicketkeeper concedes many runs, yet is still trusted to bear the burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lets ... drop' moves the T further down: STUMPER becomes SUMPTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sumpter is an old word for a packhorse or mule, an animal made to carry burdens.

clue.text: A policy to have 50% of kids injected with a hormone

indicators.note: the half-word and the A are put inside A and the policy

parts.note: a line is a policy or stance, as in the party line

indicators.note: half of the word for kids is kept, its first four letters going

parts.note: kids is informal for children

explanation.surface: A health policy requires half of all children to receive a hormone injection.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' keeps the back half of the word for kids; 'injected' puts that and the A from 'with a' into the first A and the policy, leaving 'to have' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands in moments of stress or excitement.

clue.text: Plant is submerged under Italian river with the passing of time

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first
the letter for time passes away, removed from the river

parts.note: the Tiber flows through Rome

explanation.surface: A plant lies sunk beneath a river in Italy as the years go by.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberis is the botanical name of candytuft, a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Fungus in food briefly stored under stove

indicators.note: in a down clue the food sits beneath the stove

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker

indicators.note: briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: rice is a food

explanation.surface: Mould found on food kept under the kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: An agaric is a mushroom-type fungus with gills, such as the fly agaric.

clue.text: Mathematical chart has number attached to cat and sheep

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farm diagram showing how many cats and sheep there are.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomogram is a graphical calculating diagram, a chart of scales for reading off results.

clue.text: Record-holder's short rest before historic victory

indicators.note: puts the cut-down word for rest ahead of the victory
short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: sleep is rest
VE is Victory in Europe, the 1945 Allied victory

explanation.surface: A champion's brief nap before a famous triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' suggests a champion; it is the cover a vinyl record is kept in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is the cardboard cover that holds a gramophone record.

clue.text: Tail spy, missing nothing

indicators.note: missing means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a scout is a spy sent ahead to gather information
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An instruction to follow a spy, while gathering nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail' looks like a verb, to follow the spy; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Worker given discharge, twitching where it's very cold

parts.note: the ant is the standard crossword worker
an arc is an electrical discharge between two points
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A worker gets an electric shock and is left twitching out in the freezing cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the south polar region, the coldest place on Earth.

clue.text: Transport condition is indicated by this finally

definitions.meaning: to transport goods is to send them by sea or freight

definitions.text: condition is indicated by this finally
definitions.meaning: a suffix put at the end of a word to show a state, as in friendship or hardship

explanation.surface: A transport official notes that the condition is shown at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To send goods is to transport them; and the suffix -ship marks a state or condition, as in kinship.

clue.text: I worried about body of people being uprooted

indicators.note: about means turned round, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: cared means worried or was concerned
a nation is a body of people

explanation.surface: Someone frets about a whole population being driven from their homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns I CARED round to DERACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Deracination means tearing up by the roots, especially displacing people from their homeland.
